subject: Cooking
title: Indian Chai: The Spiced Revolution
description: A fast breakdown of Indian Chai: The Spiced Revolution for builders.

hook.text: India produces more tea than any country except China. But Indians didn't drink tea until the British forced it.

buildup.text: The British East India Company pushed tea consumption in India to create a domestic market for their plantations.

discovery.text: Indians resisted plain black tea. They added milk, sugar, and spices — cardamom, ginger, cinnamon — inventing masala.

twist.text: Chai wallahs (tea vendors) became India's street food backbone — an estimated 1 million chai stalls operate nationwide.

climax.text: India now consumes 70% of its own tea production — a market the British created but Indians completely transformed.

punchline.text: The British brought tea to India. India made it chai. The world followed.

quiz.question: How did masala chai originate?
options: Indians added milk and spices to British-imported tea they initially resisted

details.summary: Indian chai is strong black tea simmered with milk, sugar, and spices — typically cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves. The British established tea plantations in Assam and Darjeeling to break China's tea monopoly, but Indians transformed British tea culture into something uniquely theirs.
details.whyItMatters: Chai shows how a colonially imposed commodity gets reinvented by the colonized culture. India took British tea, added its own spices and traditions, and created something entirely new.
takeaways: British established Indian tea plantations to break China's monopoly
Indians added spices, milk, and sugar to create masala chai
Chai wallahs on every corner make it India's most democratic drink

faq.question: Why did Indians add spices and milk to tea?
faq.answer: Early Indian tea was often made from low-grade dust and fannings left after export-quality leaves were shipped to Britain. Spices, milk, and sugar masked the harshness and transformed it into something delicious.

faq.question: What makes a good masala chai blend?
faq.answer: A strong base of CTC Assam tea stands up to milk. Fresh crushed cardamom and ginger are essential. Cinnamon, cloves, and black pepper add warmth. The tea must be simmered with milk and spices — not steeped separately. Every family has preferred proportions, and no two blends taste alike.
